name: buck
description: Buck converter power stage, 12 V to 5 V at 2 A
assumptions: CCM, ideal switch and diode, 30% ripple
Generic switch/diode models; verify with the real controller and FET
Loop compensation, EMI and thermal design are not modelled

requirements.text: Convert a nominal 12 V DC input to a nominal 5 V DC output.
requirements.acceptance: Spec declares VIN=12 V and VOUT=5 V.

requirements.text: Supply a 2 A nominal output load.
requirements.acceptance: Spec declares IOUT=2 A and a 2.5 ohm nominal load.

requirements.text: Provide editable circuit and simulation deliverables.
requirements.acceptance: Generate SPICE, LTspice, KiCad schematic/netlist, BOM and report artifacts.

architecture.summary: Non-isolated asynchronous buck-converter power-stage model using an ideal controlled switch, freewheel diode, inductor and output capacitor.

decisions.rationale: The requested output is lower than the input; a buck topology is the appropriate step-down architecture.

decisions.decision: Use ideal switch and diode models for the first-pass example.
decisions.rationale: This keeps the example runnable without proprietary device models; it is a topology demonstration, not a production-ready component selection.

risks.risk: Ideal switch and diode models do not capture real semiconductor losses, switching behavior or safe operating area.
risks.mitigation: Select a controller, MOSFET and diode from current datasheets; replace generic models and calculate worst-case stresses before hardware use.
risks.verification: Run vendor-model simulation and verify voltage, current, thermal and SOA margins at input/load/temperature extremes.

risks.risk: The example does not design feedback compensation, startup, current limiting, EMI or thermal management.
risks.mitigation: Treat the example as a power-stage scaffold only; add control-loop, protection and thermal design before implementation.
risks.verification: Complete loop stability, transient, fault, conducted/radiated EMI and thermal tests on the final design.
